News.title: Teen who groomed girl, 14, using online game Roblox is jailed after sickening campaign of abuse
News.content:
ONLING ABUSE Teen who groomed girl, 14, using online game Roblox is jailed after sickening campaign of abuse

A CREEP who used Roblox to groom a schoolgirl has been jailed after a sickening campaign of abuse.

Carlo Tritta, 19, used “flattery, gifts and rewards” to control a 14-year-old girl after meeting her on Roblox.





He has been jailed for 28 months after pleading guilty to a range of child sex offences.

Tritta groomed the child – who cannot be named for legal reasons – and took explicit photos of her for over a year.

When the girl’s mum became so concerned that she went through her phone, she was shocked to uncover a sick trove of messages.

The girl, who cannot be named, “thought she was in loving relationship but it was founded in coercion, control and abuse”.



But Tritta sent persistent messages to the girl, encouraging her to send sexually explicit images of herself back in return.

Tritta and the girl first met on Roblox in September 2024, and two months later, she told him she was 15.

He then convinced her to move their conversations onto Discord and Snapchat.

In December 2024, she admitted she was actually 14.



He led her to believe they were in a relationship, sending her gifts and takeaways, love-bombing her and constantly calling or messaging her.

When the girl’s mother became aware, she contacted police and Tritta was arrested in August 2025.

He was bailed with strict conditions not to contact the girl or her mother while police seized his phone and began an investigation.

But the obsessive creep proceeded to contact the girl’s friends through social media, called and texted the girl multiple times and even sent her two cards via Moonpig.com trying to encourage her to drop the case.

This behaviour escalated when Tritta reported the girl’s mother to child services, and contacted police trying to get the investigating officer removed from the case.



He has been sentenced to jail for making indecent images of a child, sexual communications with a child and causing a child aged 13-15 to watch a sexual act.

He also admitted two counts of intimidating a witness and criminal damage.

Passing sentence at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court, Judge Kieran Rankin said: “It was clear to you very early on that she was under 16.

“Your behaviour has had a significant negative effect on [the girl] and her family.”

Det Supt Kenny said: “The young girl in this case thought she was in a loving relationship but it was founded in coercion, control and abuse and the offender’s main driver was to obtain indecent images of her as a child.



“He used a number of methods to do that – flattery, gifts, rewards.”

Last year, Roblox said it is making it harder for dangerous predators to chat with children online by introducing a new age check.

The move comes amid disturbing incidents reported within one of the world’s most popular video game, including claims of online sex parties, bullying and grooming.

Now all gamers will have to submit a selfie to work out their age, blocking adults from being able to message minors.

Users will only be able to chat to those in their assigned age group or “similar age groups as appropriate”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Gamers in Australia, New Zealand, and the Netherlands will be the first who have to prove their age.

Others countries including the UK and US will follow this year.

News.title: Trump ‘demands Nato ships steam into Strait of Hormuz in DAYS’ as alliance pushed to brink in dream come true for Putin
News.content:
DONALD Trump is reportedly demanding Nato forces send warships to unlock the Strait of Hormuz and take on Iran within the next few days.

Top European diplomats fear Trump is offering a major ultimatum to the alliance demanding that they fight alongside the US in the Middle East or risk America pulling out of Nato in a dream-come-true scenario for Vladimir Putin.





Several diplomats were reportedly briefed on Trump’s claims after he held top-secret talks with Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte in Washington on Wednesday, according to Der Spiegel.

It comes as

They claimed the talks mentioned Nato partners being asked to commit military forces to the Strait of Hormuz to support Trump’s war and to help reopen the key trade route.



Rutte is expected to brief European leaders telling them about Washington’s demands, the report claims.

Trump reportedly expects concrete commitments from all members of the alliance and is asking them to send warships or military capabilities to the Middle East.

The US president is believed to have told Rutte he can no longer rely on speeches of commitment from heads of state and now needs real action.

Many allies have been hesitant to directly involve themselves in the war despite Trump’s constant pleas for support over the past five weeks.



Appearing to confirm the report, Trump hit out at the alliance today saying that Nato was coming under “pressure” to act.

He said: “None of these people, including our own, very disappointing, Nato, understood anything unless they have pressure placed upon them!!!”

A Nato spokesman added that the US expected “concrete commitments and action to ensure freedom of navigation in the strait”.

The fracturing alliance will delight Vladimir Putin who could see a severely weakened Europe as ripe for conquest.



If allies refuse to deploy warships to the Middle East then it could be the final nail in the coffin for Nato.

Trump could follow through with his threats to abandon the alliance and leave entirely – taking away America’s unrivalled funding and huge firepower.

The US is among only a handful of global militaries that can claim to be stronger than Russia, with no other nation in Nato coming close.



This could leave Europe vulnerable to Russian cyberattacks or physical meddling.

Nato could go and support Trump, however, sending across their best military assets to help wrestle the global economy back under control by helping with Hormuz.

This could also have dire consequences as it would leave nations without their most advanced warships, which would be best suited to fend off a potential Russian attack.

UK Defence Secretary John Healey warned today that Russia has increased its activity across Europe while the eyes of the world are on the Middle East.

It comes after allied intelligence monitored a Russian attack submarine and two spy submarines lurking near undersea cables and pipelines in the North Atlantic.



It comes amid backlash aimed at the Royal Navy after the UK was hesitant to send any warships out to the Gulf to help with the war against Iran.

Starmer eventually sent out HMS Dragon after days of umming and ahhing which drew a fiery response by Donald Trump over a lack of support.



Addressing the concerns over Britain’s capabilities, Healey said the lurking danger posed by Russia meant the UK couldn’t lose focus of defending its own interests.

He said: “I understand people questioning why all UK military assets and personnel have not been deployed to deal with it, but that is not in Britain’s national interest.

“The greatest threats are often unseen and silent, and as demands on defence rise, we must deploy our resources to best effect.”

It comes after reports claimed Trump is mulling over plans to punish “unhelpful” Nato nations who haven’t been helpful to the US in the war.

Trump may begin to pull troops out of certain countries and move them to more “supportive” allies, according to the Wall Street Journal.



It remains unclear what nations could be on Trump’s chopping block but he has shared fiery exchanges with leaders such as Britain’s Keir Starmer and Spain’s Pedro Sanchez in recent weeks.

The German government has signalled its willingness to take part in a joint mission in the strait in recent days.

But they say guarantees must be made first, including the promise of a ceasefire or Iran agreeing to a negotiated truce.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz even criticised the US and Israel for lacking a clear strategy to end the conflict after a two-week ceasefire lasted mere hours this week.

What has sparked the US-Nato rift? DONALD Trump has gone on several furious tirades against Nato ever since launching Operation Epic Fury at the end of February on Iran. Most of these verbal attacks feature the US president accusing his allies of not supporting him during the war. He has been vocal about wanting help from Nato warships – especially the UK – to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blocked off. Trump blasted Nato allies as “cowards” after they refused to send ships to the Middle East. He said on Truth Social: “NATO NATIONS HAVE DONE ABSOLUTELY NOTHING TO HELP WITH THE LUNATIC NATION, NOW MILITARILY DECIMATED, OF IRAN.” The war has also caused Trump to engage with Nato leaders such as Britain’s Keir Starmer and Spain’s Pedro Sanchez. Trump called Sir Keir “no Winston Churchill” as he slammed the UK PM for his reluctance over letting the US use Brit bases to attack Tehran. He then threatened to halt all trade with Spain after PM Sanchez declared he would bar the US from using its military bases as part of operations in Iran. “We don’t want anything to do with Spain,” he added. Even before the war in Iran kicked off, Trump hit out at Nato as he claimed some allies “stayed off the front lines” in Afghanistan. The alliance responded by reminding him that hundreds of allied troops were killed fighting shoulder-to-shoulder with US forces. The war in Ukraine has also been a major point of difference within Nato. Trump claimed last September Nato has never been 100 per cent committed to ending the conflict – as he tried his best to hash out a peace deal. He ordered the alliance to apply the pressure on Putin as he even promised: “If Nato does as I say, the WAR will end quickly, and all of those lives will be saved!”

The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz remains a top priority for all nations who rely on the global trade route for goods such as oil.



Iran had unblocked the waterway for a few hours before they closed it again after Israel blitzed their allies in Lebanon.

The regime has now released a chilling map showing how tankers will be forced to weave through deadly sea mines dotted throughout the Strait.

Jab’s at Nato have also come from White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt as she quoted Trump as saying: “Nato was tested and they failed.”

She added that it was “sad that Nato has turned their backs on the American people”.

Rutte was asked if he agreed that allies had failed the US, to which he replied: “Some of them yes, but a large majority of European countries, and that’s what we discussed today, have done what they promised before in a case like this.”



The secretary general, known in Europe as the “Trump whisperer”, has constantly tried to calm down concerns of an unfixable rift among Nato members.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said he had a “frank and open” discussion with Trump on Wednesday as he told CNN: “Not all European nations lived up to those commitments, and I completely understand he is disappointed about it.

“I was also able to point to the fact that the large majority of European nations has been helpful.”

News.title: Moment man chases down and punches group of kids after they ‘attacked his car’ sparking huge brawl
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a man chases down and appears to punch a group of kids after they allegedly attacked his car.

The youths can be heard screaming and shouting as a mass brawl breaks out in the street in Belfast, Northern Ireland.





Video of the altercation went viral, with viewers claiming the youths “attacked” the man’s car prior to the punch-up.

Tensions initially begin to mount as the kids surround the car at the beginning of the clip and appear to throw objects at it.

Some of the youths are then shown in a tense exchange with a man and woman in the vehicle – before it stops in the middle of the road.

The man – believed to be the passenger – then jumps out, before sprinting towards and squaring off with a number of the youngsters.

A crowd of teens quickly amasses around him, before the woman ushers him back into the car.

Seconds later, a youth then seems to throw something at the car, prompting the man to once again chase after him.

He disappears from view, before exchanging words with other members of group and returning to his motor.



But, just as the situation seems to be calming down, something else appears to be launched at the car – reigniting the feud.

Moments later, the man – wearing a grey t-shirt and black cap – then darts towards the retreating crowd for a third time.

Tempers flare as he chases some of the teens down the road, while shouting can be heard in the distance.

After following some down another road, they all reappear and the man appears to throw punches towards some of the youths.

A mass brawl ensues as the alleged attacker continues to land blows on the kids, with some seen trying to push him away.



The drama unfolded near Shankill Road on Tuesday evening.

Cops later received reports of anti-social behaviour and assaults in the area.

Northern Ireland Police confirmed officers were aware of the incident, with enquiries underway.

The force said: “Police are conducting enquiries into a number of reports of anti-social behaviour and assaults in the Shankill Road area of Belfast on Tuesday 7th April.

“Enquiries into the matter are currently ongoing.”



It comes after footage emerged of a heroic driver ramming an alleged machete-wielding “thief” as he reportedly attempted to steal a motorbike.

Video showed the motorist using his Land Rover to tackle the suspected crook in a busy car park outside a Sainsbury’s in Brixton, South London.

Shocked onlookers can initially be heard shouting as the 4×4 reverses out of a space, before driving towards the alleged thief.

The driver then crashes into the helmet-clad rider, forcing him off the motorbike as he seemingly tries to escape from the Tulse Hill Sainsbury’s.

News.title: Hero pal stabbed trying to save friend, 21, knifed to death in brawl at beauty spot as dad reveals why he was there
News.content:
THE hero pal of a 21-year-old knifed to death at a London beauty spot was also stabbed while trying to protect his friend during the brawl.

Finbar Sullivan tragically died after being stabbed at the popular viewing point on Primrose Hill, North London, on Tuesday evening.





Cops rushed to the scene, having received reports of a fight at around 6.40pm, where they discovered Finbar with stab wounds.

He was sadly pronounced dead at the scene, with his heartbroken dad Christopher describing it as “the worst tragedy I could ever imagine”.

The 65-year-old told how his son had gone up to the hill to do some filming with a new camera before his tragic death.

Christopher also revealed Finbar had been with his friend who bravely tried to protect him and was himself attacked in the process.

His pal was stabbed in the back and hands as he attempted to fend off the attackers, before being rushed to hospital.

Christopher told MailOnline: “They went up there because it was a nice day. My son met his friend and he was also stabbed.

“He was stabbed in the back and in the hands as he was trying to protect him (Finbar).”



The Metropolitan Police said no arrests have so far been made.

It remains a mystery why the 21-year-old was targeted in the scenic park, which was packed with people enjoying the warm sunny weather.

Shocking video footage circulating on social media seems to show a knife fight breaking out in the park.

At least three men dressed in grey and black start brawling in front of shocked onlookers.

One appears to have a knife and lunges at a man dressed in grey, who is seen with what appears to be blood on his top and backs away.



The other two men are then shown running down the path away from the scene.

Christopher said his son was not part of a gang, adding he was a “studious kid” who spent his time watching films and editing videos.

The devastated father said his son, could never be replaced, had been the victim of an “indiscriminate stabbing”.



He added: “It’s Primrose Hill, for God’s sake… it’s like Hyde Park. It’s not somewhere you expect this.”

Finbar had followed in his father’s creative footsteps, studying at the London Film Academy.

In recent years he filmed and produced music videos for UK drill rappers.

One of the artists he had worked with, GGL Wuni, paid an emotional tribute to Finbar.

He wrote: “My brother, my family, I will never let your name fade.



“The most clean-hearted guy I’ve ever met, always turned up for me without a miss.”

Det Insp Andy Griffin said: “Finbar’s family have suffered a devastating loss and our thoughts are with them as they navigate this very challenging time.

“Our investigation is progressing at pace and we are following several lines of inquiry.

“This incident occurred in a busy, public park and there may be many witnesses who can help us piece together what happened.

“We are aware of footage circulating on social media around the time of the incident.



“We urge anyone who has any information, including photos or videos, which could support the investigation to urgently contact us.”

Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart told locals that “there will be an increased police presence in the area over the coming days”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes after 16-year-old schoolboy Harry Pitman tragically died after being stabbed in the neck in the same park on New Years Eve in 2023.

He was murdered by fellow teen Areece Lloyd-Hall, who was jailed for at least 16 years for the Harry’s death.

News.title: Cat and dog ‘flown to safety by Ukrainian drone to save them from advancing Russian troops’
News.content:
A CAT and dog were flown to safety by a Ukrainian drone to escape advancing Russian troops on the front line, according to reports.

The animals are said to have travelled eight miles for the mercy mission coordinated by Ukrainian fighters.





Food supplies had been flown in to soldiers of the 14th Separate Mechanised Brigade defending Ukraine’s frontline near Kupyansk, in the Kharkiv region.

On the return flight, they evacuated the two animals from a zone threatened by Vladimir Putin’s invading forces.

Astonishing footage shows the pair being pulled from bags after reportedly completing the daring flight.



“Well, I’ve never flown on a drone before,” a Ukrainian man said to the cat.

Adding: “You’ll be ours. Ah, she is already purring, she is content.

“Of course she flew, she flew, she is very happy.

“We’ll give you food, some proper food to eat.”



Before the rescue mission the cat was being cared for by a Ukrainian soldier.

But when the service man was injured in combat and rushed to hospital, his pet was at risk of being abandoned in the volatile war zone.

His comrades decided to rescue the animal — and could not leave the dog behind either.

Animal welfare organisation UAnimals said: “Soldiers of the 14th Mechanised Brigade evacuated a cat and a dog from a position using a drone.

“Risky? Yes, but leaving them there was even more dangerous, and there was no other way to get them out.



“The cat and dog flew 12 kilometres [7.5 miles] — they are safe and now with the soldiers.

“We thank the defenders for saving the most vulnerable.”

This is not the first time Ukrainian troops have mounted a dramatic rescue mission for animals during war.

Lioness Yuna was flown out of war-torn Kyiv in 2023.

The three-year-old had been brought to Ukraine’s capital illegally and kept trapped in a four metre by three metre cage on concrete.



When war broke out, she was stranded without food as bombs dropped around her.

But in January 2023, Yuna was chanced upon by military volunteers searching homes in the city.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They alerted Natalia Popova, from Ukraine-based Wild Animals Rescue Center, whose team drove through the country’s capital while it was under siege to save Yuna.

Handlers sedated and loaded the lioness into a truck to transport her to their nearby sanctuary.

News.title: Politician expelled from party for releasing VERY different-looking publicity pic – but she insists ‘that really is me’
News.content:
PHOTO FINISHED Politician expelled from party for releasing VERY different-looking publicity pic – but she insists ‘that really is me’

A POLITICIAN was expelled from her party after releasing a digitally altered image that looks nothing like her, even as the 59-year-old insists that the photo “really is me”.

Patricia Reichman published the photo in a local newspaper as part of an election campaign to sit on the council of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.



But when the Dutch politician was elected last week, constituents quickly realised that the woman before them looked nothing like the photo in her campaign materials.



The released image shows a young blonde woman who looks several decades younger – and several layers more airbrushed – than the real Patricia Reichman.

Reichman claims she edited the photo because it was too low resolution to run in the print.

She said: “I ran it through an online tool to boost the pixel count. It really is my photo; that really is me”.

She added: “I look a bit different at the moment, but that is due to medication I’m taking. That will be ending soon.”



The photo shows airbrushed skin, glossy blonde waves and darkened eyes.

Despite intense skepticism and backlash to the image, the 59-year-old insists that she usually looks very young for her age and is often mistaken as her son’s girlfriend.

She concedes: “I look much younger in that one photo”, referring to the edited image.

“But normally I look very young for my age too. When I’m out with my son, people think I’m his girlfriend. I hear very often that I look very young for my age,” she added.



Unfortunately for Reichman, her political party has not bought the excuse.

“When the information provided during the job interview proves not to correspond with reality, there is no basis of trust to continue working together,” the Leefbaar Rotterdam statement reads.

“The photo has clearly been heavily edited with AI and is not a realistic representation.”

The party initially asked the councilwoman to resign, but Reichman refused.

Leefbaar Rotterdam, which translates to ‘Livable Rotterdam’, then revoked Reichman’s party membership and expelled her.



The outrageous debacle has sparked amusement online.

“Practically twins”, quipped one person on Instagram.

“‘Boosted the pixel count’ to what? Another reality?” joked another.

“There’s always a reasonable explanation for everything, she’s a natural politician,” another quipped.

“That’s not even the same eye colour,” a user pointed out.



“Sure, it’s the ‘medication’ that makes her like 59 in real life. Not the fact that she is 59,” another added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another recent photo editing scandal saw a white influencer shamelessly edit her own face onto the body of a black model.

The image was clearly completely ripped off the rival influencer and published as if it was a new photo taken at the US Open.

News.title: Tragic autistic girl, 7, drowned in golf course pond after she ‘escaped childminder through gap in park fence’
News.content:
A TRAGIC seven-year-old girl was found drowned on a golf course after she escaped her childminder through a gap in the fence, an inquest heard.

Nyla May Bradshaw was found dead in a pond in South Yorkshire last month after she was reported missing.





Her mum Hayley reportedly left the autistic youngster with a specialist SEND childminder but just two hours later, she received a text saying Nyla had vanished.

An inquest heard today “during the course of the day she was taken out to a park in the Owston area of Doncaster”.

Nyla then passed through a hole in a fence and headed towards nearby woodland.

Coroner’s officer Jane McDonnell said a search was launched after the childminder raised the alarm with police and the youngster’s family.

She was later found unresponsive and face down in a pond on Owston Hall golf course in Doncaster.

Nyla was rushed to Doncaster Royal Infirmary but was tragically declared dead at 1.18pm.

Senior coroner Nicola Mundy adjourned the full inquest at Doncaster Coroner’s Court until December 8.



Family friend Charlotte Emma said the Ofsted-registered childminder had been told that Nyla was a “flight risk”.

She explained the youngster’s mum left Nyla with the new babysitter, who was “recommended over Facebook”, as her regular minder was fully booked.

Devastated parents Hayley and Kieran Bradshaw paid tribute to their daughter online.

In a heartbreaking post on her Facebook page, Nyla’s mother wrote: “It breaks my heart to write this, but today we lost our beautiful daughter Nyla May Bradshaw at just 7 years old.

“She was our whole world full of love, laughter, and the brightest smile that could light up any room.



“She brought so much joy into our lives and into the lives of everyone who knew her.”

Her dad Kieran Bradshaw described her as his “best friend” and an “amazing daughter”.

He wrote on Facebook: “You were so loved Nyla you touched everyone’s heart that ever met you.

“I’ll never ever go a moment without you in my thoughts.”

News.title: Boy, 11, shot in head by pal when gun they found in woods accidentally went off
News.content:
GUN SCARE Boy, 11, shot in head by pal when gun they found in woods accidentally went off

A BOY has been injured after being accidentally shot by a gun he and a pal had found in the woods.

The 11-year-old was with a friend in Weston, Southampton when they found what they initially thought to be a BB gun.





Police said that upon finding the firearm and taking it home, it was accidentally discharged.

Remarkably, the boy escaped without serious injury and was only treated for a graze to his head.

It was later confirmed that the BB gun was actually a pistol and the incident was reported to cops at around 5.30pm on Tuesday evening.

An area at Westwood Nature Reserve has been cordoned off after officers were escorted to where the gun was discovered.

Chief Inspector Chris Douglas, deputy district commander for Southampton, said: “As soon as this incident was reported to us on Tuesday, our teams were swiftly in attendance and have been carrying out thorough enquiries and searches in the area since.

“We know that our scenes will have disrupted people’s normal daily routines, and we want to thank local residents for their patience as we carry out our investigation.

“Thankfully, this discovery has not resulted in more serious injuries, and the boys and their families have acted quickly to report the matter to us and allow us start further enquiries.

“These kinds of firearms are often used to threaten people, and cause serious harm, and we are committed to tackling and disrupting serious criminal activity.



“Our teams remain in the area today, and will be conducting patrols and house to house enquiries, if you do have any concerns or questions, then please do not hesitate to speak with them.”

News.title: London Waterloo live: Clapham Junction train delays as person dies on tracks
News.content:
Emergency services rushed to an incident between London Waterloo and Clapham Junction where a person died - causing major disruption for train passengers

Passengers are facing major disruption after a person died on tracks by London Waterloo station.

Emergency services are currently dealing with an incident between London Waterloo and Clapham Junction, forcing all lines to close.

Trains are being cancelled or delayed by up to 90 minutes, and the chaos is expected until the end of the day. Stations including Surbiton have been closed as a result - with passengers seen gathering outside trying to find alternative routes.

News.title: Brooklyn Beckham's suspicious question to wedding planners shortly before sacking
News.content:
Brooklyn Beckham's suspicious question to wedding planners shortly before sacking

It's been four years since Brooklyn Beckham tied the knot with Nicola Peltz - and their wedding remains one of the most talked-about celebrity nuptials for all the wrong reasons

View 5 Images Brooklyn and Nicola will be celebrating this week (Image: B4859 / Avalon)

Brooklyn Beckham and Nicola Peltz are celebrating their fourth wedding anniversary after a year of drama.

‌



The couple tied the knot at the Peltz family's sprawling oceanfront estate, Montsorrel, in Palm Beach, Florida.

‌



It was a lavish affair, with a star-studded guest list and no expense spared as the couple exchanged their vows in front of their family and friends. But, as the world now knows, there was a whole lot of drama going on behind the scenes.

‌



One major setback came six weeks before the wedding took place when celebrity planner Preston Bailey stepped down. He later told Page Six that he was "overcommitted" and therefore "couldn't deliver the quality I was used to".

Beckham family distance themselves from Brooklyn with wedding singer move READ MORE :

Nicola Peltz shares intimate message Brooklyn Beckham left her as she slept READ MORE :

View 5 Images Brooklyn and Nicola tied the knot on 9 April 2022

Planning duo Nicole Brahin and Arianna Grijalba from Plan Design Events were quickly brought on board in his place. But they inherited what they later described as a 'crime scene', according to The Cut.

‌



"The previous planners had created a wedding website that allowed guests to RSVP for as many people as they wanted. Invites had gone out to some and not others from guest lists that were incomplete and out of date. There were still vendors to be booked."

The two women were also inundated with new requests, including a water dance floor, flowers suspended in ice and a baby-pink colour palette at the after-party.

View 5 Images The wedding was held at the Peltz family's 13-acre oceanfront Palm Beach estate, Montsorrel (Image: LCD/Shutterstock)

‌



Aspiring chef Brooklyn had his own contributions - specifically relating to the Wendy’s burger truck that would be serving late night food to guests. He was said to have requested a 'Brooklyn burger' and a 'Nicola burger', the latter using lettuce instead of a bun.

He is also said to have suspiciously asked if they should consider getting a "gun that shoots a net because there's probably gonna be drones".

Ultimately, the partnership with Brahin and Grijalba was short-lived. The planners were fired nine days before the wedding and in December 2022, Nelson Peltz filed a lawsuit, tstaing that he had not received his $159,000 deposit back.

‌



The billionaire’s lawyers claimed in the lawsuit: "The celebrity of the wedding couple combined with the anticipated attendance of many high-profile guests required that the wedding planner have the expertise and staffing to plan, coordinate and execute a wedding event of the expected caliber and complexity.”

View 5 Images Brooklyn and Nicola with her father, Nelson Peltz (Image: INSTAGRAM)

The lawyers continued: "Peltz had presented them with the opportunity of a lifetime – to have their names associated with the wedding of two world-famous celebrities, which would undoubtedly propel PDE into wedding planning stardom.”

‌



“In reality, however, it later became clear that [Braghin and Grijalba] viewed this is as an opportunity to take advantage of Peltz by making material misrepresentations on both their website and in person regarding their experience, expertise, and capability of planning the wedding,” the lawsuit alleged.

In response Braghin and Grijalba filed a countersuit against the billionaire in February 2023, citing breach of contract. They requested that Peltz pay them $50,000 (£37,250) in damages, plus legal costs, and argued that while they were experienced event organisers, the Peltz family were challenging to work with.

They claimed: “Both Claudia and Nicola had insisted that Victoria Beckham (Brooklyn’s mother) could not know about any internal mistakes regarding the ongoing planning of her son’s wedding, including any errors with the guest list.”

‌



View 5 Images Brooklyn is no longer in contact with his parents (Image: Zak Hussein / SplashNews.com)

The document also stated: “It is believed that Nelson Peltz paid more than $100,000 plus travel expenses for Nicola’s hai and makeup services for the wedding. Claudia mentioned to Braghin [a wedding planner] that Nelson could not know the cost of the hair and makeup, or he would ‘kill her, and be so mad’.”

In March 2023, Nicola and Claudia then filed a new motion to be removed from further legal proceedings following "malicious and mean-spirited" allegations.

Article continues below

The drama eventually came to an end in September 2023 when the parties released a joint statement that read: "The parties believe that this contract dispute between Nelson Peltz and Plan Design should be resolved on the terms agreed. As part of the settlement, PDE will make a donation in the name of Nicola and Brooklyn to the CARE Ukraine Crisis Fund. PDE wishes Nicola and Brooklyn Peltz Beckham happiness and a fruitful life together."

The family ended up hiring third wedding planner Michelle Rago of Michelle Rago Destinations to help pull the event together.

News.title: Schoolboy, 11, shoots himself in the head after mistaking pistol for BB gun in UK woods
News.content:
Schoolboy, 11, shoots himself in the head after mistaking pistol for BB gun in UK woods

Hampshire Police Chief Inspector Chris Douglas said investigators rushed to a wooded area in Southampton after the boy's near miss with the gun, which he and a friend had brought home

View 4 Images Police remain on the scene following the incident this week (Image: DE/Solent News)

A young boy was shot in the head after finding a pistol in the woods he and a friend mistook for a BB gun - but miraculously escaped without serious injuries.

‌



The schoolboy, 11, walked away with nothing more than a graze to the head after he and another boy discovered the deadly weapon in a wooded area near Tickleford Drive in Weston, Southampton, on April 7. Parts of a nature reserve in the area, Westwood Nature Reserve, have remained cordoned off for days, and police remain at the scene today.

‌



Hampshire Constabulary confirmed as investigators continue to comb the area that the pair had brought the gun home, believing it was a BB pistol - play guns that shoot pellets instead of bullets - before accidentally firing it once.

‌



Primrose Hill stabbing brawl as hero friend tried to save pal after being knifed to death READ MORE :

View 4 Images Police are combing the wooded area where the gun was found (Image: DE/Solent News)

Police said they were alerted to the situation just before 5.30pm that evening, and were taken to the area where the gun was found by the children. Chief Inspector Chris Douglas, deputy district commander for Southampton, said investigators rushed to the areas and have been thoroughly searching the area in the two days since.

He said: "As soon as this incident was reported to us on Tuesday, our teams were swiftly in attendance and have been carrying out thorough enquiries and searches in the area since."

‌



View 4 Images The gun was discharged by one of two boys at an address in Wadhurst Gardens (Image: DE/Solent News)

"We know that our scenes will have disrupted people's normal daily routines, and we want to thank local residents for their patience as we carry out our investigation. Thankfully, this discovery has not resulted in more serious injuries, and the boys and their families have acted quickly to report the matter to us and allow us start further enquiries.

"These kinds of firearms are often used to threaten people, and cause serious harm, and we are committed to tackling and disrupting serious criminal activity." The boy was treated for a graze to the head following the gun discharge.

Article continues below

View 4 Images Locals have been urged to speak to police if they have questions (Image: DE/Solent News)

Police have confirmed that it was the boy who wasn’t injured that fired the gun. Police have said that investigative teams have remained in the area following the incident, and are currently carrying out house-to-house inquiries. Locals who may have concerns regarding the news have been encouraged to speak with officers who remain on the scene.

Chief Inspector Douglas said: "Our teams remain in the area today, and will be conducting patrols and house to house enquiries, if you do have any concerns or questions, then please do not hesitate to speak with them."

News.title: KitKat truck flanked by security convoy after 12-tonne chocolate theft
News.content:
KitKat truck flanked by security convoy after 12-tonne chocolate theft

After the great KitKat heist on March 29, the confectionary brand have taken no risks with their lorries transporting the chocolate bars as a branded KitKat lorry was seen travelling with a police convoy

View 2 Images The lorry was seen in a police convoy

With 12 tonnes of KitKats missing - the brand are taking no risks anymore and have called in additional help.

‌



A recent KitKat branded lorry was seen driving on the motorway surrounded by a police convoy after thieves stole more than 400,000 bars from a truck travelling between Italy and Poland. Both the chocolate bars and the truck carrying 12 tonnes of chocolate vanished and remain missing still.

‌



KitKat's parent company Nestle said they are working with local authorities and supply partners to investigate. They released a statement on the heist and said: "The vehicle and its contents remain unaccounted for, and investigations are ongoing in close collaboration with local authorities and supply chain partners."

‌



KitKat heist of 400,000 bars sparks warning over chocolate shortage at Easter READ MORE :

View 2 Images Over 400,000 KitKat's were stolen in the heist (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

It's estimated there were 413,793 bars stolen, but each one is traceable with their batch numbers on the pack, prompting KitKat to ask anyone who finds a match to alert the company."

Playing on the KitKat slogan, Nestle further added: "We've always encouraged people to have a break with KitKat. But it seems thieves have taken the message too literally and made a break with more than 12 tons of our chocolate.

‌



"Whilst we appreciate the criminals' exceptional taste, the fact remains that cargo theft is an escalating issue for businesses of all sizes. With more sophisticated schemes being deployed on a regular basis, we have chosen to go public with our own experience in the hope that it raises awareness of an increasingly common criminal trend."

Now in Canada, a truck with high security escorts was spotted on Wednesday (8 April), but it's unclear if this was a stunt by KitKat after the logstical nightmare quickly turned into a marketing internet sensation for other brands. Memes began to spread by wildfire, as brands including British Airways, Dominos and Ryan Air chimed in.

Dominos shared a post on Instagram announcing a brand new topping, and making a joke out of the situation. They said: "We would like to announce our thoughts and condolences with Kit Kat following their recent sad news.

Article continues below

"On a completely unrelated note, we're pleased to announce we'll now be selling a new Kit Kat pizza." While British Airways shared a post with an image of a KitKat container being loaded onto a plane with the statement: "Our thoughts are with KitKat at this difficult time.

"Separately, today we are moving a record-breaking volume of chocolate" sparking a viral response from followers finding the joke amusing.

The stolen chocolate bars were from the brands new Formula One line, as KitKat was announced as the official F1 chocolate bar. The chocolates were racecar shaped, but Nestle warned the stolen bars could "make their way into unofficial markets".

News.title: Primrose Hill stabbing brawl as hero friend tried to save pal after being knifed to death
News.content:
Primrose Hill stabbing brawl as hero friend tried to save pal after being knifed to death

The dad of filmmaking student Finbar Sullivan said his son had likely died after trying to stand up for someone, adding: 'Maybe the attacker was bullying someone'

View 4 Images Finbar Sullivan died on Tuesday (Image: PA)

A filmmaking student who was stabbed to death in a north London park was shielded by a hero pal who sustained injuries while he tried to protect him.

‌



Finbar Sullivan, 21, was pronounced dead at the scene of a horror attack in Primrose Hill on Tuesday after he was allegedly stabbed in a fight near the tourist-heavy beauty spot at around 7.30pm. His dad, Christopher Sullivan, has revealed he had gone to the park to use a camera he was given for his birthday when the "beautiful, lovely, outgoing, loving boy" died.

‌



Mr Sullivan also revealed that a friend of his son's had been stabbed in the back and hands as he tried to protect him, and that he believed he was trying to "stand up" for someone.

‌



View 4 Images Finnbar has been remembered as a 'beautiful' man by his dad (Image: Enterprise News and Pictures)

The dad told the Daily Mail: "His friend was stabbed in the back and hands trying to protect him. My son always tried to stand up for people, so maybe the attacker was bullying someone.”

The Metropolitan Police have urged “anyone who has any information, including photos or videos”, and the dad has described the incident as the "worst tragedy I could ever imagine". He said: “He’s my only son… I had him when I was 45. He can never be replaced. He’d just bought a new camera, we all chipped in for his 21st birthday, and he took it up there to do a bit of filming.”

‌



Mr Sullivan, a musician and founder of 1980s band Blue Rondo a la Turk, added: “I’m so broken-hearted, I can’t believe it. He was the most beautiful, lovely, outgoing, loving boy. He was just a really lovely person."

View 4 Images Met Police investigators have urged people to come forward if they have information about the incident (Image: Enterprise News and Pictures)

“And why he was targeted, we have no idea.” Mr Sullivan said he rushed to Primrose Hill as soon as he was informed of the incident – of which police said on Wednesday video footage was circulating online.

‌



“I got the call at about six that he’d been stabbed, so I rushed up there,” Mr Sullivan told the Mail. “I wasn’t allowed in because it was a crime scene, and by that point he’d had 20 minutes of CPR. He’d obviously died. “It’s Primrose Hill, for God’s sake… it’s like Hyde Park. It’s not somewhere you expect this.”

Finbar Sullivan was a student at the London Screen Academy and produced music videos for drill rap artists under the name Sully Shot It, the Mail reported. Despite the drill rap scene’s association with gang violence, Mr Sullivan denied his son was involved in any of it.

View 4 Images Finbar's dad said his son was 'the subject of an indiscriminate stabbing' (Image: INSTAGRAM/nzsocietyuk)

Article continues below

He said: “All I can tell you is he was the subject of an indiscriminate stabbing. He was not a gang member. He was just a little groovy 21-year-old who loved movies and making films. He didn’t drink, he didn’t smoke, he didn’t go out. He’d stay at home editing his films six nights a week. He wanted to follow in his (grandfather’s footsteps) and be a cameraman.

“He recently did a video for Joseph Corre, Vivienne Westwood’s son. We were just about to start a company together… he was going to do his showreel today with me. And now he’s dead.”

During the fight on Tuesday, a second man in his 20s also injured and taken to hospital for non life-threatening stab wounds, police confirmed. The Met added in their appeal that no arrests have yet been made in connection with the incident.

News.title: Brit Jermaine Grant remanded in custody after being accused of 'leading Al-Shabaab terror platoon'
News.content:
Brit Jermaine Grant remanded in custody after being accused of 'leading Al-Shabaab terror platoon'

Jermaine Grant is accused of committing a number of offences, including directing the activities of terror group Al-Shabaab, attending a commando training camp and two counts of possession of an AK47 for terrorist purposes

View 3 Images Jermaine Grant, 43, has been charged with a total of six alleged offences, including directing the activities of the organisation (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

A British man has been remanded in custody after appearing in court accused of being a platoon leader for Somalia-based terror group Al-Shabaab.

Jermaine Grant, 43, has been charged with a total of six alleged offences, including directing the activities of the organisation between December 31, 2007, and January 1, 2009, three counts of attending an Al-Shabaab commando training camp in Kismayu, Somalia, and two counts of being possession of an AK47 during battles.

Grant appeared at Westminster Magistrates Court on Thursday afternoon, where he spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth. He was wearing a green and yellow jumpsuit while being flanked by two police officers standing either side of him wearing baseball caps. At least two more police officers stood guard in a corridor behind the dock. Asked by the judge if he has an address, he replied: "No".

Prosecutor Carl Kelvin told the court: "Grant went to Al-Shabaab training camps, trained as a commando, became a platoon leader, took part in a number of battles and discharged firearms and took full part in fighting." District Judge Nina Tempia remanded Grant in custody to appear at the same court via video-link on April 16. It is understood the move is in order to give the Attorney General time to decide whether to prosecute.

View 3 Images Al-Shabaab is an Islamist armed group that has been linked to al Qaida (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

All of the offences are said to have committed by Grant while he was allegedly part of Al-Shabaab, which was proscribed as a terrorist organisation by the UK government in March 2010. The group has previously claimed responsibility for a number of attacks, including the Westgate shopping mall atrocity, which left 67 people dead in Nairobi, Kenya, in September 2013 and became notorious for recruiting foreign fighters, allegedly including 'White Widow' Samantha Lewthwaite.

Westminster Magistrates Court heard Grant, who was born in London and is a British citizen, was allegedly an Al-Shabaab fighter and attended a specialist commando training camp before engaging in battles and being promoted to a platoon leader between 2008 and 2009.

Prosecutors also claim that between December 31, 2007, and January 1, 2010, he was involved in the Battle of Mogadishu Stadium, where he was allegedly armed with an AK47. He is also accused of being armed with an AK47 at the Battle of Karan between December 31, 2007, and January 1, 2010.

If found guilty of directing a terrorist organisation under Section 56 of the Terrorism Act 2000, Grant would face life imprisonment. The other charges he faces, including attendance at a place used for terrorist training and possession of articles for terrorist purpose, both carry sentences of 10 years in jail.

View 3 Images The accused appeared at Westminster Magistrates Court on Thursday afternoon (Image: PA)

The charges came after an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London. Acting commander Kris Wright said: "These are serious charges and come as the result of a long-running investigation. This case shows we will always pursue anyone suspected of being involved in terrorist activity, no matter where in the world or how long ago it is alleged to have taken place."

Head of the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter terrorism division Frank Ferguson, said: "We have decided to prosecute Jermaine Grant with directing the activities of a terrorist organisation, three counts of attending a place for terrorist purposes and two counts of possession of an article for terrorist purposes.

Article continues below

"The charges relate to Mr Grant's alleged involvement in 2008 and 2009 with Al-Shabaab, a terrorist organisation operating in Somalia. Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court and that it is in the public interest to pursue criminal proceedings.

"We have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police's Counter Terrorism Command as it carried out its investigation. We remind all concerned that criminal proceedings against this defendant are active and that he has the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings."

Al-Shabaab is an Islamist armed group that has been linked to al Qaida. The organisation was labelled a "persistent threat" in Somalia's capital, Mogadishu, which carries out "high profile attacks that challenge government authority", according to a 2025 assessment by the UK Government. It has targeted international aid workers, journalists, business people and non-government organisations who have opposed or resisted it.

News.title: NHS urges people to 'look for code' when buying common item and 11am to 3pm rule
News.content:
NHS urges people to 'look for code' when buying common item and 11am to 3pm rule

The warm weather will send many Brits to the shops in search of the summer accessory

View 3 Images The NHS urges people to be careful in the sun (Image: Getty)

With the weather warming up, Brits are making the most of the sunshine with park picnics, BBQs, and long walks. However, it's important to stay safe in the sun, and the NHS offers advice on protecting your skin and eyes.

‌



As most people know, sunburn increases your risk of skin cancer. The NHS explains: "Sunburn does not just happen on holiday. You can burn in the UK, even when it's cloudy. There's no safe or healthy way to get a tan. A tan does not protect your skin from the sun's harmful effects."

‌



People should also take care to protect their eyes. While it might be less well known, people who don't look after their eyes can also suffer sunburn-like damage.

‌



"A day at the beach without proper eye protection can cause a temporary but painful burn to the surface of the eye, similar to sunburn," warns the NHS. "Reflected sunlight from snow, sand, concrete and water, and artificial light from sunbeds, is particularly dangerous."

As such, it's recommended to wear clothes and sunglasses that provide sun protection, such as a wide-brimmed hat and wraparound sunglasses. On the NHS website, the health authority says shoppers can look for a code to ensure they're buying sunglasses with adequate protection.

View 3 Images The health service shared the importance of protecting your eyes (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

‌



The NHS recommends looking for 'sunglasses with wraparound lenses or wide arms with the CE Mark and British Standard Mark 12312-1:2013 E.' It's especially important to follow the advice between 11am and 3pm from March to October, when the NHS says the sun is at its strongest.

According to Specsavers, the CE mark shows that the sunglasses meet EU safety requirements. Offering advice for customers on its website, the opticians said: "You can tell whether sunglasses offer UV protection by checking if the frame features the CE or UV400 mark.

"The category for the lens shade (0-4) should also be marked on the frame, for example, ‘C3’ followed by ‘CE’. The CE mark shows that the sunglasses conform with the health, safety and environmental requirements of the EU, and therefore offer a good amount of UV protection for your eyes."

Article continues below

View 3 Images People should also take care to protect their skin from the sun (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

Specsavers added that customers should not confuse the darkness of the lenses with UV protection. The experts explained: "It’s important to remember that the darkness of your sunglasses lenses has nothing to do with UV protection — it only helps to reduce the brightness of light that reaches your eyes.

"You’ll still need to ensure that your sunglasses have certified UV protection in order to keep them safe from damage." More advice is available on the Specsavers website.

News.title: Morning Joe hosts stunned by JD Vance’s ‘messed up’ comments about his wife
News.content:

The hosts of MS NOW’s Morning Joe were left scrambling for words as they struggled to make sense of JD Vance’s eccentric analogy comparing Iran’s right to enrich uranium with his wife’s freedom to skydive.

The VP, visiting Hungary in support of the country’s nationalist leader Viktor Orban ahead of Sunday’s elections, was asked at Budapest airport about comments made by Iran’s parliamentary speaker in which he emphasized his country’s “right to enrichment.”

Vance scoffed as he recited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf’s remark and added: “I thought to myself, you know what? My wife has the right to skydive, but she doesn’t jump out of an airplane because she and I have an agreement that she’s not going to do that because I don’t want my wife jumping out of an airplane.”

“We don’t really concern ourselves with what they claim they have the right to do. We concern ourselves with what they actually do and I think the president’s been very clear on the enrichment question. Our position on that has not changed.”

open image in gallery Vice President JD Vance compares Iran’s nuclear demands to the prospect of his wife skydiving ( Reuters )

Second lady Usha Vance announced in January that she is pregnant with the couple’s fourth child, which might have been what her husband had in mind when expressing his opposition to her attempting daredevil stunts, although he did not say so.

Reacting to footage of his comments, Morning Joe presenter Mika Brzezinski found it difficult to hold herself together, saying: “I’m just – I really don’t want to hear about women’s rights, and rights and women from JD Vance.”

“If that’s your takeaway…” her co-host and husband Joe Scarborough interjected.

“Don’t start the morning that way,” Brzezinski responded. “So messed up.”

“That was such a confusing analogy, my teeth hurt right now,” Scarborough joked. “I’m still trying to figure it out.”

“Yeah,” added fellow contributor Willie Geist. “I also didn't know you were allowed to give your wife rules of things she can’t do. I need to write a few down now on how we operate!”

“Women across America have rules that I never grew up with that kill them, so that’s where we are,” Brzezinski added.

open image in gallery Morning Joe presenters Mika Brzezinski and Joe Scarborough grapple with Vance's eccentric analogy ( Morning Joe/MS NOW )

Vance was speaking after the U.S. had agreed a late ceasefire deal with Iran, which was brokered by Pakistan Tuesday, just in time to stop a fresh round of airstrikes.

But the temporary truce already looks to be in jeopardy over disagreement about whether or not Israel’s campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon is included in the two-week suspension of hostilities.

Preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon is one of several stated aims of Operation Epic Fury offered by President Donald Trump, despite his claiming to have “obliterated” the country’s enrichment facilities in a previous bombing campaign last summer.

Prior to those attacks, Tehran had enlarged its stockpile of uranium enriched to near weapons-grade levels, according to a confidential report by the United Nations’ International Atomic Energy Agency obtained by the Associated Press.

open image in gallery Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has insisted on his country’s right to pursue its nuclear aspirations ( Getty )

However, nuclear energy need not necessarily be devoted to building weapons of mass destruction. It can also be used to generate electricity, provide drinkable water through seawater desalination, and is used in medical treatments.

Just before Vance launched into his skydiving analogy, a reporter had asked him whether the country might be allowed to continue enriching uranium for “civilian nuclear purposes.”

He answered that by saying: “What the president has said is that we don’t want Iran to have the capacity to build a nuclear weapon.

“The president has also said that we don’t want Iran enriching towards a nuclear weapon and we want Iran to give up the nuclear fuel. Those are going to be our demands during the negotiation.”

News.title: This one move could save your financial life from drowning in debt
News.content:
For many borrowers, debt can be summed up in nine words: easy to get into, hard to get out of.

Americans collectively owe $18.8 trillion - the majority in housing debt (mortgages, home equity loans and the rest) and $5.2 trillion in credit cards and loans, according to the Federal Reserve. This works out at $94,000 per U.S. adult, on average.

Being burdened with debt can be a harrowing experience, particularly amid the current high cost of living.

“Those pressures weigh on their mental health, and when they don’t have the means to make ends meet, they may turn to credit cards, and racking up a balance they can’t repay causes stress and anxiety,” said Leslie H. Tayne, a personal finance expert and founder of Tayne Law Group.

For those struggling with debt, there’s one important step that could pull them out of a financial hole: taking inventory of what’s owed.

open image in gallery ‘A lot of people make having debt part of their identity, which leads to them experience shame and helplessness,’ one expert said ( AFP via Getty Images )

Know your numbers

The most important first step in overcoming debt is to get down in writing all the accounts you owe money to, experts said.

“I would suggest the first step to getting out of debt is to gain a true understanding of their current debt load,” Mary Sasmaz, an assistant professor in Case Western Reserve University’s accountancy department, told The Independent.

A borrower should make a written list of all their debt - personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, auto loans, student loans, medical bills, and buy-now-pay-later plans. Write down the following numbers for each account, Sasmaz explained:

Balance

Borrowing rate

Monthly payment.

Typically, you can find each of these data points in your most recent statement or by logging onto your online account.

“This is what I call the ‘in the know stage’, which takes a lot of effort, but it’s essential to building a plan and starting to move forward,” Tayne told The Independent. “You simply have to know what you are working with to really begin.”

To be thorough and make sure your debt-clearing journey gets off to a good start, set aside time to gather these numbers when distractions are minimal, Tayne said. Bringing your family and even good friends into the process can be a huge help, too.

“Ask for help from a trusted friend or family member if it feels overwhelming,” she said. “When you have someone dedicated to helping you, it can feel supportive, which eases the mental burden, but also helps keep you accountable and make sure the task gets done.”

Meaningful mindsets

While debt is a numbers game, it’s the conversation in a borrower’s head that can have a significant impact on how successfully they are at paying off what they owe.

So, while taking inventory of all your debt accounts is the most important step in the process, pairing that step with sound mindsets will help borrowers continue in their debt-payoff journey.

Separating your identity from the debt is one of those mindsets, said Prisca Benson, owner of money coaching practice Our Green Life.

open image in gallery Knowing what is on the other side of that finish line is also important mental motivation, said one expert ( Getty Images )

“A lot of people make having debt part of their identity, which leads to them experience shame and helplessness,” Benson told The Independent in a query. “When people shift their mindset so that debt is a part of their story, not their entire story, they can then approach it with a clear and focused mind.”

Knowing what is on the other side of that finish line is also important mental motivation, said Ashley Morgan, a bankruptcy attorney and owner of Ashley F. Morgan Law, PC.

“Do you want to use that extra money toward a vacation? A new car?” Morgan said in an email to The Independent. “Having a goal can make it easier to continue when things get difficult.”

Focus on the “why” behind debt payoff, said Kristine Stevenson Seale, owner of tax resolution and financial coaching firm Proverbs 16:16 LLC (a biblical reference to the importance of wisdom over wealth).

“It's very important to know why you want to get out of debt,” Stevenson Seale told The Independent in an email. “You'll be tempted along the debt-free journey, and if your 'why' is strong enough, you can resist the temptation to spend. Without digging deep into the why, your desire and ability to become debt-free can be derailed.”

open image in gallery Keep focused on the “why” of your debt repayment is a good motivator, one expert said ( PA Archive )

That “why” could include breaking generational cycles of debt, improving mental health or freeing up money to build retirement savings.

If a borrower achieves becoming debt-free, the feeling is fantastic - but the whole cycle will start over if they don’t identify what initially put them in a financial hole, Sasmaz said.

“Paying off debt can be euphoric - feels like a weight taken off - but care must be taken to identify habits that may have led to significant debt in the first place so that the individual does not find themselves in a cycle of debt creation requiring significant debt management again and again,” she said.

News.content:

Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a domestic storm over the two-week ceasefire with Iran, with critics accusing him of presiding over “the worst political disaster in history”.

The Israeli prime minister has sparked backlash from parties across the country’s political spectrum for choosing not to continue the conflict alongside Donald Trump.

There is also growing international outcry over ongoing Israeli strikes on Lebanon, that as of Thursday had killed 1,700 people, including 130 children. Western countries have insisted Lebanon must be part of the ceasefire, while Tehran claimed that attacks on the country represented a "grave violation" of the agreement.

open image in gallery Netanyahu is increasingly isolated on the world stage ( AFP/Getty )

The developments have sparked outrage among Israeli politicians, who have urged Netanyahu to continue the war. Opposition leader Yair Lapid branded the Israeli PM’s handling of the conflict a catastrophe.

“There has never been such a political disaster in all of our history,” he wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. “Israel wasn’t even at the table when decisions were made concerning the core of our national security.”

He praised the military for carrying out “everything that was asked of it” and the public for demonstrating “amazing resilience”, but said they had both been let down by Netanyahu due to what he called the leader’s “arrogance, negligence and lack of strategic planning”.

Lapid’s criticism was repeated by former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who said Israel’s failure to achieve its war goals would leave it “facing a vengeful Iran.”

“The reason why so many people feel disappointed tonight is that the leadership sold us illusions,” he said in a live broadcast on Wednesday.

“All their empty promises have exploded in our faces. Unfortunately, each of us sees with our own eyes that Hamas is getting stronger. Hezbollah and Iran are standing on their own two feet, and this is happening because a government that dismantles Israel from within cannot defeat the enemy from without.”

Yair Golan, centre-left politician and the head of the Democrats party, accused Netanyahu of lying.

“He promised a ‘historic victory’ and security for generations, and in practice, we got one of the gravest strategic failures Israel has known,” he said in a post on X, adding: “Blood was spilled ... brave citizens killed (and) soldiers fell ... none of the goals were accomplished.”

open image in gallery Lapid has called Netanyahu’s strategy a ‘historical disaster’ ( AP )

“The nuclear program was not destroyed; the ballistic threat remains; the regime is in place and is even stronger coming out of this war," he continued.

Netanyahu’s education minister Yoav Kisch hit back his critics, accusing them of “pumping up a defeat that’s echoed in the enemy’s media outlets”.

The Israeli PM has also faced growing international outcry over the IDF’s campaign in Lebanon, which aid agencies warn has created a humanitarian catastrophe. Over 250 people have been killed in 24 hours in the deadliest attacks on the country since the conflict began.

More than 100 sites were targeted in 10 minutes on Wednesday and more than a million people (20 per cent of the population) has been displaced since the war began in February.

Despite a ceasefire being agreed on Wednesday, Netanyahu and the White House said that the 14-day truce does not apply to Lebanese territory - a key demand for Tehran.

open image in gallery Netanyahu and Trump both acted jointly in declaring war on Iran ( Getty Images )

But Netanyahu and the White House said that the ceasefire does not apply to Lebanese territory.

Israel says it must continue its attacks in order to defeat Hezbollah, an Iran-backed proxy group. However, large numbers of civilians have been killed so far and humanitarian groups have warned there are similarities to the IDF’s campaign in Gaza.

Spain, France and the UK have all called for the ceasefire to be extended to Lebanon.

Britain’s foreign minister Yvette Cooper called for the country to be “urgently included” and called Israel’s attacks “highly damaging” on Thursday, following similar comments by French president Emmanuel Macron.

The European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas criticised the number of civilian deaths in Lebanon and said it was becoming “hard to argue that such heavy-handed actions fall within self-defence”.

open image in gallery Over 200 people were killed in one day in Lebanon on Wednesday after Israel’s deadliest strikes yet ( Reuters )

Trump has also come under fire in Israel for agreeing a ceasefire.

“Donald, you came off as a duck,” said the far-right head of the country’s National Security Committee, Tzvika Foghel in a since-deleted post on X.

The head of the conservative Yisrael Beytenu party, Avigdor Liberman, said the agreement with Iran “gives the ayatollah’s regime a break and time to regroup.”

“Any agreement with Iran, without giving up on destroying Israel, enriching uranium, manufacturing ballistic missiles and supporting terror groups in the region, means we’ll return to another war in harder conditions with a heavier price,” he wrote on X.

It’s not a bird or a plane - it’s a “flying” fish - and the airborne invaders are causing chaos for fishermen and boaters across the Midwest.

Asian carp have taken over the Mississippi River and many of its tributaries, reshaping waterways and even injuring people. By consuming massive amounts of food that native species rely on, these invasive fish throw ecosystems off balance, making life harder for both local fish and the anglers who depend on them.

Originally introduced in the 1970s for aquaculture and algae control, these non-native silver and bighead carp are especially notorious in the Midwest for their jumping behavior. Startled by boat vibrations or noises, they can launch more than 10 feet into the air, according to U.S. Geological Survey researchers, sometimes colliding with unsuspecting skiers, paddlers and boaters, causing injuries.

The unusual threat has prompted political action in states such as Michigan and Illinois, where lawmakers are pushing for measures to contain the carp population. Proposed solutions include building physical barriers and deploying sound devices to repel the fish from busy waterways. Yet many residents have turned to their own strategies to stay safe.

Peoria firefighter Nate Wallick told the Wall Street Journal about the lengths he goes to protect his family while tubing on the Illinois River.

“I took one right in the side of the head,” he said. “The fish darn near knocked me out.”

Asian carp can leap up to 10 feet when startled, forcing Midwest fishermen to get creative to keep themselves and their families safe on the water ( T. Lawrence, Great Lakes Fishery Commission )

Wallack told the outlet that he now makes his children wear football helmets, has built a cage around their inner tube, and has equipped everyone on his boat with nets, he said. He also takes precautions for himself while water skiing, wearing a helmet and cup after a carp once struck him in the groin.

Clint Carter said he was recently boating and had a carp leave a bone bruise that took weeks to heal, according to the Journal. His friend, however, took more of a punishment.

“It actually hit him between the eyes, dropped him to his knees,” Carter said.

Efforts to control the carp have been underway for decades, using physical barriers, electric deterrents, bubble curtains and sound repellents. Funding delays and logistical challenges, however, have left many waterways vulnerable.

Communities have also embraced unconventional solutions. The Redneck Fishing Tournament in Bath, Illinois, for example, encourages participants to net jumping carp as a recreational challenge, helping to reduce numbers in targeted areas, the Journal reported.

The state’s Department of Natural Resources even launched a marketing campaign to rebrand the fish as “Copi,” short for copious, to set them apart from the less desirable bottom-feeding common carp, encouraging people to eat them. Fishermen and chefs say the carp are surprisingly tasty, though their bony structure makes them difficult to serve as traditional filets. To work around that problem, chefs often grind the fish and use them to make dishes such as fish cakes, according to the outlet.

Wildlife agencies also recommend cautionary measures for residents, including slowing down near ramps and docks, keeping a distance from other vessels and ensuring passengers stay seated in central areas of the boat.

Golfing legend Gary Player has urged Tiger Woods to stop driving while reliant on pain medication, following the 15-time major winner's recent arrest for driving under the influence (DUI).

Woods is seeking treatment, believed to be in Switzerland, after being charged with driving under the influence last month following a car crash near his Florida home.

Police found two prescription opioid hydrocodone pills in his pockets at the time of his arrest, which the golfer has been using to manage chronic pain after numerous significant operations.

Nine-time major winner Player expressed deep sympathy for Woods’ physical difficulties but pleaded with him not to get behind the wheel of a car again.

"The human being is so critical of everything but my heart goes out to him," Player said. "There’s nothing worse than living in pain every day of your life. You can’t think of anything worse."

open image in gallery Gary Player has offered advice to Tiger Woods (AP Photo/David J. Phillip) ( AP )

He continued: "Do I blame him for taking medicine? Hell, no. He has sleep deprivation. Do I blame him for taking something to help him sleep? No. But I don’t think he should drive a car.

“When you’re taking that medicine it’s dangerous when you’re driving a car, same as it’s dangerous when you look at your cell phone in the car. All he’s got to do is just not drive a car and get a chauffeur. My reflexes, I think, are as good as when I was 20, but I don’t drive anymore. I get a chauffeur. I think that’s the answer to it."

Player expressed his hope that Woods, now 50 and eligible to play on the Champions Tour where the physical demands are less, could make a successful return to the sport where he has built such a legacy.

"I just hope he can get it all sorted out because he’s such an asset to golf and has done so much for the game," he added.

Jack Nicklaus, whose 18 majors Woods chased but now will never catch, also offered his support.

Asked for a message for Woods, he said: "Just (get) whatever you need to help you and get back, because I think golf needs him, and we’d love to have him back."

Nicklaus was one of a trio of former Masters champions, alongside the 90-year-old Player and 76-year-old Tom Watson, who hit ceremonial tee shots to officially start the 90th Masters at Augusta.

The golf legend admitted the shot, surrounded by a packed gallery, was a worry for him and he will only continue in the role for as long as he does not "kill anybody".

The late Arnold Palmer retired from the ceremony in 2015, aged 86, due to physical limitations.

open image in gallery Jack Nicklaus hit a ceremonial tee shot at the Masters on Thursday ( PA Wire )

Nicklaus, who will be 87 at next year’s event, had his son Jackie tee the ball up "so I don’t fall over".

He recounted his concerns about the shot: "I said ‘Spread out on both sides because I don’t want to kill anybody. If it had been a little closer, I might have. I got it high enough to hit it about 110 yards over their heads on the left.’"

He concluded: "I don’t know what was running through my mind other than not hurt anybody. I had carpal tunnel surgery about five, six weeks ago, and I was worried about not being able to hold onto the golf club and hurt somebody.

“But it’s such a nice ceremony and a real honor to be invited I hope to be able to do it as long as I can not kill anybody."

News.title: Five essential things to know before you board a Disney Cruise Line ship
News.content:
Disney brought its enchanting brand of magic to the high seas by way of Disney Cruise Line in 1998, with Captain Mickey Mouse at the helm. The fleet has since grown to eight ships, which resemble floating versions of the entertainment giant’s famous theme parks, packed with fun and full-on entertainment programmes.

Elegant décor and classical styling brings an upmarket feel that gives a nod to the golden age of sea travel, and extends Disney’s appeal to grown-ups who can enjoy the surprisingly extensive child-free areas on each ship. Onboard attractions – water-coaster rides, nightly Disney-themed musicals, artwork that bursts into life and a real-time talking turtle – exemplify the innovative twists this legendary brand is renowned for.

These frills translate into cruises which are generally higher priced than other family-friendly lines, but such is the cost of tapping into a world where onboard experiences are sprinkled with fairy dust.

News.title: From lockdown to Los Angeles: the rise and rise of South Sudan’s blind footballers
News.content:
Like many great and unusual ideas the inspiration for founding South Sudan’s first blind football team came during lockdown.

It was 2020 and Simon Madol Akol was looking for ways to help the disability inclusion charity Light for the World when he discovered the sport. Able to see himself, he had no idea that it could be played by people without vision. But the opportunity was there.

“This is possible,” he remembers thinking. “This is something that can be done.”

The team’s beginnings were humble, but it was always ambitious. Named the Bright Stars – just like South Sudan’s national team – at the start it had just two players.

One of them was current captain Martin Lado, who was born with limited vision but remembers promising himself to pour energy and focus into the team, hoping that “one day it will make us proud”.

From these origins, the team has gone on to win an international championship in Uganda and is now training for the Paralympics.

But all this was yet to come, and first, they had to learn the rules of the game.

News.title: Liverpool refuse to wave white flag, but don’t bet on another famous comeback
News.content:
Van Dijk, who has won eight major trophies during his eight years with Liverpool, said that the team had let down both their manager and the fans, before pointedly adding: “But also you shouldn’t give up, and that’s maybe what happened at a certain point.”

Upon arriving at the Parc des Princes for their Champions League quarter-final first leg against defending Paris St Germian, Wirtz was also asked if the players still had faith in Slot, whose position has come under enormous scrutiny following Saturday’s defeat. With the gap to Arsenal in the Premier League now 21 points, the Champions League is Liverpool’s last remaining hope of a trophy this season.

Asked if they were still playing for the manager, Wirtz said: “Yes of course we are believing in the manager. The team should believe in the manager because they won the league last season. We have a lot of good games this season.”

Slot himself was more nuanced in responding to Van Dijk’s comments, claiming that Liverpool had actually played well in going toe-to-toe with Manchester City for the opening 35 minutes. “Usually in football moments that hurt you most are just before half time and just after half time,” said Slot of City’s burst of goals between the 39th and 57th minute.

“[At 3-0] I saw indeed five minutes in between where it was too open and players were struggling. After the 4-0, City seemed to be OK with the 4-0. We had the ball. Not able to create that much any more. I didn’t see players giving up in the part of the game

“But I think it’s also good from a captain that he has a strong and firm reaction after a game like that. Hopefully it’s not only immediately after a game and we can as a team show a strong and firm reaction.

“[It was] the only four chances we gave away in the game by the way. The good thing is that during this year we have become quite experienced in terms of negativity because of all the setbacks we have had this season.”
